text:
elaine: quick sync — i pushed a prototype for implicit session affinity + fallback proxy. short thread with tradeoffs and a config sketch.

sam: nice. is this the approach that keeps state in the runtime or in a separate policy service?

elaine: current prototype keeps only lightweight affinity keys in runtime (sticky header `X-Canary-ID`) and asks a policy service for routing & fallback decisions. runtime enforces circuit-breakers locally.

priya: can you paste the config you used?

elaine: sure — super small example:
```yaml
rollout:
  type: canary
  split:
    baseline: 80
    canary: 20
  session_affinity: implicit  # formerly explicit cookie-based
  affinity_ttl: 10m
  fallback:
    policy: prefer-baseline
    error_threshold: 0.03  # 3% 5xx over probe window
    latency_threshold_ms: 350
    probe_window: 60s
```

jordan: looks clean. how do you measure quality regressions (not just 5xx/latency)?

elaine: good call — we tag a small eval traffic slice and compute a similarity delta vs baseline using the eval set. policy service exposes `quality_delta` along with `error_rate` and `p50` when making routing decisions. if quality_delta > 0.04 we bias traffic back to baseline.

sam: where does the affinity key come from? request ID? user ID?

elaine: prefer deterministic user-id if present, else short-lived request affinity generated by the router. goal is to avoid re-routing halfway through a conversation.

priya: sounds stateful — is that going to break autoscaling? what about mem pressure on the runtime?

elaine: we keep it small: only store a 64-bit affinity token per session in local LRU with TTL. worst-case falls back to stateless routing if mem pressure high.

ops-bot: note: affinity cache misses are instrumented as `affinity.miss` metric.

jordan: interesting tradeoff: stateful affinity improves model-consistency but complicates failover. what happens if the canary instance crashes mid-session?

elaine: router attempts to recover by checking policy for last-known preference; if unavailable, it replays to baseline by default. that's the explicit failover behavior.

sam: how expensive is the policy lookup on every request? latency-sensitive paths can't block on an RPC each token.

elaine: policy responses are cached with TTL ~1s in runtime. decision API returns lightweight rule + reason code. runtime evaluates local fast-paths for common cases (e.g., global override, emergency throttle).

priya: any thoughts on long-term refactor? I remember the RFC suggested pushing more logic to the control plane.

elaine: yeah — long-term idea: ship policy rules and a compiled decision table to the runtime. runtime becomes mostly offline-evaluating and stateless for the hot path; control plane handles complex diagnostics, rollout strategies, and training the quality heuristics.

jordan: that aligns with scaling. also would help with infra isolation for Private deployments.

sam: risks?

elaine: 1) consistency: compiled rules can lag; 2) complexity: two codepaths (live-decision vs compiled); 3) telemetry - need richer labeling to debug why a session fell back.

priya: we should add a rollout meta header `X-RD-Decision: canary|baseline|forced-fallback` for tracing.

elaine: agreed — added to prototype. also added a short reason code: `reason=quality_regression` or `reason=runtime_failure`.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for model `open-llm-v2` (canary=20%). Monitor endpoints: /metrics and /rollouts.

sam: can we automate an emergency rollback when combined signals cross thresholds? (latency + quality + error).

elaine: yes — policy supports composite rules: e.g. `if error_rate>0.02 and quality_delta>0.03 then full-roll-back`. runtime honors `force_fallback` boolean and flips split to 0 for canary.

jordan: one more ask — include a debug endpoint to query `affinity->active_variant` for a session id, that will speed postmortems.

elaine: good call. i'll add `/debug/session/:id` returning `variant, ttl, last_seen, reason` (debug only).

priya: lgtm. next steps: write a lightweight RFC follow-up with the decision table format and the telemetry contract. i'll volunteer to draft.

elaine: thanks! i'll clean up the prototype and link the RFC in the thread. :thumbsup:
